cards.def: A devastating epidemic of bubonic plague, a bacterial disease spread by fleas on rats, that killed a large share of Europe's people.
A large kingdom unified under a strong central monarch who directly controls its territory, taxes, armies, and laws.
A light, narrow sailing ship with triangular lateen sails that could sail against contrary winds and handle rough Atlantic seas.
A navigational instrument that measures the angle of the sun or a star above the horizon so sailors can calculate their latitude at sea.
The long Christian campaign to drive Muslim rulers out of the Iberian Peninsula and restore Christian rule over Spain.
A Spanish soldier-adventurer who led or joined the armed conquest of American peoples in search of gold, land, and glory.
The transfer of plants, animals, people, and diseases between the Americas on one side and Europe and Africa on the other that followed Columbus's voyages.
An outbreak of a disease among a population that has never been exposed to it and therefore has no acquired immunity.
The European portrayal of Spanish colonial rule as uniquely cruel, greedy, and murderous toward the Native peoples of the Americas.
The religious movement that attacked the Catholic Church's corruption and papal authority and split western Christianity into Catholic and Protestant churches.
A Catholic pardon, often sold for money, that promised to shorten a soul's punishment in purgatory for sins already committed.
The Protestant belief that people are saved only through faith in God's freely given grace, not by performing good works.
The Protestant belief that every Christian can read and understand the Bible and approach God directly without depending on priests.
The Calvinist belief that God decided before creation which people would be saved and which would be damned.
In Calvinist belief, the people whom God has chosen in advance for salvation, whose disciplined lives might show signs of that choice.
In Calvinist belief, the worldly occupation God assigns each person, in which disciplined work and service to others honor God.
A monarch's written grant giving a person or company the right to explore, settle, govern, and profit from overseas territory.
The Algonquian title for a chief who ruled a group of villages and collected tribute from them in return for protection and leadership.
